Elena — thanks, outline below and attached. Short version: we prefer an endorsement (ISO or insurer-specific) that names Redwood Inference, Inc. as Additional Insured on a primary & non-contributory basis for Commercial General Liability (CGL). Waiver of subrogation in favor of Redwood is required for Workers' Comp only where permitted by law.

Attached: Redwood_Insurance_Specs_v2.docx (checklist + acceptable alternatives) and endorsement_template_primary_noncontrib.pdf (fillable sample).

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- CGL limits: $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate (minimum)
- Excess/umbrella: $3,000,000 (combined) preferred depending on deal size
- Professional liability / E&O: $2,000,000 for SaaS integrations (if applicable)
- Additional Insured: Redwood Inference, Inc.; address: 650 Castro St, Mountain View, CA 94041
- Primary & non-contributory language explicitly stated on endorsement
- COI is acceptable for intake but must be followed by insurer endorsement within 15 business days; if endorsement not possible, an insurer letter with policy number, effective dates and confirmed coverage can be considered for limited onboarding (legal sign-off required)

If your broker can email mark.hooper@acme-brokerage.com to our broker intake (broker@redwood-inference.com) with a timeline we can expedite. If they plan to send an insurer letter instead of an endorsement, please include expected date for full endorsement or underwriter contact.

Next steps: please have broker send interim COI + expected endorsement ETA. I'll loop in Legal internally to confirm the insurer-letter fallback.

-Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the summary. Short answers + proposed playbook below.

1) Insurer-letter fallback: Acceptable as interim evidence only where the letter is on carrier letterhead, signed by an underwriter, and contains the policy number, limits, effective/expiry dates, and a statement that an endorsement adding Redwood Inference, Inc. as Additional Insured (primary & non-contributory) will be issued within X business days. We recommend X = 10 business days for small customers, 15 for enterprise deals. If the endorsement does not arrive within the window, treat as a contractual non-conformance and escalate to finance/legal hold.

2) Waiver of subrogation: We require a waiver of subrogation in favor of Redwood only for Workers' Compensation where permitted by law. Do not require blanket waiver on CGL unless underwriting compels it.

3) If carrier refuses to name Additional Insured: Options (in order of preference):
   a) Accept endorsement on a primary & non-contributory basis — preferred.
   b) Accept endorsement that names Redwood as "Additional Insured - to the extent of the vicarious liability arising from the Named Insured's acts" — only if accompanied by higher limits or umbrella coverage and documented insurer confirmation.
   c) As a last resort, accept COI + contractor covenant to indemnify & defense, but only with a specific contractual carve-out in the Order Form allocating indemnity for claims arising from vendor performance.

Operational playbook:
- Intake: accept interim COI + insurer declaration. Create a compliance ticket with due date = 15 business days.
- Legal review: if insurer indicates refusal to endorse, request written confirmation from underwriter and escalate to me.
- Finance: place invoice hold after 15 business days if endorsement outstanding.

I'll attach a redlined endorsement template (endorsement_template_primary_noncontrib.pdf) and a short checklist you can share.

- Aditya
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachments: endorsement_template_primary_noncontrib.pdf
